title: P0 hosted API - hedge multifanout & queue compaction postmortem
summary: On 2029-08-03 at ~15:14 UTC we experienced a P0 outage affecting hosted-api streaming and short-request paths. Symptoms: p99 token latency spiked from ~120ms to >3.5s, sustained 5xx error rate on streaming sessions (up to 8% of requests), and elevated worker queue depth for GPU inference backends. The immediate customer impact was degraded streaming experience (choppy or stalled streams) and a small fraction of failed generation requests. Root cause: a hedging change combined with an edge-proxy queue compaction interaction amplified request fanout and caused bursty KV cache pressure and downstream scheduling stalls. This doc records timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations, and required runbook changes.
impact: Approximately 12 minutes of severe degradation for ~4% of customer sessions in US and EU regions. 5xx spike peaked at 8% (baseline ~0.1%). P99 token latency increased to >3.5s; overall tokens processed reduced by ~18% due to failed/aborted sessions. Major enterprise customers experienced visible streaming truncation and a handful opened support tickets; no data loss was detected.
detection_summary: Alerting was triggered by streaming error-rate SLI (>1% 1m), then an automated Triage runbook page was created. First pager went out at 15:17 UTC. On-call noticed abnormal increase in edge-proxy retransmits and worker queue depth dashboards. Initial triage suspected a model-serving regression; further traces pointed to head-end amplification.
detailed_timeline:
15:12 UTC - Minor increase in ephemeral queue depth on edge proxies observed in telemetry but below pager threshold.
15:14 UTC - Streaming error-rate crossed 1% and alert fired; on-call created incident channel.
15:15-15:18 UTC - Engineers examined runtime logs; noticed duplicated outbound hedged requests from edge-proxy and many canceled/short-lived backends.
15:19 UTC - Evidence of compaction pass in newer edge-proxy commit that merged in a week earlier (github PR 421) which collapses idle sockets and compacts in-memory request queues.
15:21 UTC - Hypothesis: hedging + compaction => rapid retransmit/duplicate requests, amplified fanout to dedicated infra pools, causing KV cache churn and worker scheduling stalls.
15:25 UTC - Temporary rollback: edge-proxy compaction disabled in traffic config (feature flag) and hedging throttles increased to limit concurrent hedged fanout.
15:29 UTC - p99 latency and error rate trending down; streaming failures reduced to baseline by 15:34 UTC.
15:40 UTC - Incident declared mitigated.
16:00 UTC - Post-incident synthesis started and follow-ups logged.
root_cause: A recent hedging optimization intended to reduce tail latency created a scenario where the edge-proxy could issue multiple speculative requests (hedges) to downstream clusters. Separately, an edge-proxy change (queue compaction) introduced more aggressive in-memory queue reordering and socket reuse that, under the hedging pattern, caused duplicates to be replayed to backend multiplexer components. The combined effect amplified request fanout by ~3x during short bursts, which overloaded KV cache hotspots and triggered worker scheduler backpressure. That backpressure translated to long scheduling latencies and token emission stalls, producing both 5xx errors (timeouts/cancellations) and token latency cliffs.
contributing_factors:
1) Hedging default concurrency increased in rollout without region-specific canary thresholds.
2) Queue compaction feature merged behind a flag but enabled for more regions than intended.
3) Lack of a pre-merge performance microbenchmark for hedged fanout scenarios.
4) Insufficient telemetry linking hedged-request IDs to backend queue spikes (trace sampling gap).
5) Runbook did not surface decision path for hedging x compaction interactions.
mitigations_taken_immediate:
- Disabled compaction flag for edge-proxies in affected regions (15:25 UTC).
- Reduced hedging concurrency and introduced a minimum inter-hedge delay (15:26 UTC).
- Temporarily increased worker admission control limits and opened extra dispatcher capacity to allow graceful drain (15:27 UTC).
- Forced KV cache warmup on a subset of backends to reduce cold churn (15:28 UTC).
- Post-mitigation: monitored metrics for 20 minutes before declaring incident mitigated.
short_term_mitigation: Revert compaction behavior to previous safe defaults in the next maintenance window if no further regressions observed. Add an emergency feature-flag kill switch that is documented in the runbook and tested during oncall drills.
long_term_actions: Create a hedging microbenchmark suite that exercises edge-proxy compaction and backend multiplexer under synthetic fanout (owner: Daniel Park, due 2029-09-01)
Add hedged-request tracing ids through the entire serving path and increase sampling rate for fanout-related traces (owner: Liam Chen, due 2029-08-20)
Enforce region-canary gating for any features that alter request fanout or in-proxy queue behavior (owner: Marisol Ortega, due 2029-08-15)
Implement automatic hedging throttles that back off when KV cache pressure or scheduler latency crosses thresholds (owner: Priya Shah, due 2029-09-10)
Runbook update: document compaction kill-switch and explicit steps for hedging rollback during P0 incidents (owner: Aisha Khan, due 2029-08-10)
Postmortem review with product and platform teams to adjust rollout checklist to require fanout-impact analysis (owner: Eng Product, due 2029-08-17)
runbook_updates:
- Add a new section: 'Hedging + Queue Compaction' with explicit detection queries (edge hedged-request ratio, duplicated outbound IDs, KV cache churn).
- Add step: when hedged-outbound duplicates > 1.5x baseline, throttle hedges via control plane and disable compaction flag immediately.
- Document how to force KV cache warmup and scale worker dispatchers.
- Add checklist entry in pre-merge: 'hedge-fanout microbenchmark passed' before enabling compaction in a new region.
- Include links to the hedged-request trace dashboard and emergency feature flag dashboard.
retrospective_notes:
- The regression was preventable: two safe changes (hedging tweak and compaction) interacted unexpectedly. We need more cross-team pre-merge coordination for features that touch request shaping.
- Oncall response was fast and well-coordinated; the temporary mitigations restored customer experience within ~15 minutes.
- The incident highlighted a blind spot in our tracing coverage for short-lived speculative requests; fixing tracing will aid faster root cause identification in future.
- Recommend a quarterly chaos experiment that simulates hedged fanout to validate compaction and scheduler stability.
- Communications: Support drafted a customer-facing incident summary and PS team offered to proactively contact affected accounts.
notes_for_oncall:
- If you see streaming p99 > 1s and edge hedged-outbound ratio > 1.2x baseline, immediately: (1) turn on hedging-throttle in control plane, (2) disable edge compaction flag for the region, (3) scale dispatcher pool by +30% for 10 minutes, (4) open incident channel and notify eng-sre leads.
- How to disable compaction: control-plane -> feature-flags -> edge-proxy.compaction -> set to false, then verify 'compaction_active' metric goes to 0.
- How to throttle hedges: control-plane -> hedging.policy -> set max_concurrent_hedges=1 and inter_hedge_delay=250ms.
- Dashboard links: hedged-request-trace, edge-queue-depth, kv-cache-miss-rate, dispatcher-sched-latency.
- Post-incident: run the 'hedge-compaction postmortem checklist' and file follow-up tasks in JIRA with P0/P1 priority.
owner_notes: I will own the runbook change and the hedged-request tracing uplift. Team will schedule the hedging microbenchmark as high priority. We should run a tabletop with product and edge-proxy owners to rehearse the rollback steps. Thanks to the oncall crew for the quick rollback and clear play-by-play in the incident channel.
